subject.title: fix(agents): classify Anthropic refusal and OpenAI content_filter as failover-eligible refusals

question: Should OpenClaw accept a generic, opt-in cross-provider refusal fallback via `agents.defaults.refusalFallback`, or keep refusal recovery limited to provider-sanctioned paths like the merged Anthropic Fable-to-Opus fallback?
rationale: The implementation choice changes how provider safety refusals are treated and adds new config surface; code review can find defects, but only maintainers can approve this safety/product boundary.

options.title: Pause generic fallback pending approval
options.body: Keep this PR open but do not merge until a maintainer explicitly approves the cross-provider refusal fallback policy and required proof shape.

options.title: Narrow to provider-owned fixes
options.body: Reject the generic config path for now and keep using provider-sanctioned refusal recovery, with a separate narrower path for OpenAI if maintainers want one.

options.title: Approve opt-in generic fallback
options.body: Allow the new config surface after fixing the current code defects, adding sibling coverage, and posting live refusal-to-fallback proof.

recommendation.title: Pause generic fallback pending approval
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but do not merge until a maintainer explicitly approves the cross-provider refusal fallback policy and required proof shape.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged Anthropic fallback PR and linked issue comment make steipete the clearest available owner for the current policy boundary.
